'''Patricia Reiff''' (born 1950) is an American space physicist at [[Rice University]], known for her research on space weather and for engaging the public about science.

== Early life and education ==
Reiff is a self-described child of the space age and in a 2019 interview she recalls the excitement of watching [[Sputnik 1|Sputnik]] flying overhead, listening to John Kennedy's [[We choose to go to the Moon|speech about going to the Moon]], and watching the [[Apollo 11]] liftoff en route to the Moon.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|date=July 16, 2019|title=Memories of Apollo|url=https://www.rice.edu/memories-apollo|access-date=2021-07-21|website=Rice.edu|language=en}}</ref>

As a child, Reiff loved the outdoors and medicine and initially considered vet medicine as a career option. The movies produced in the [[The Bell System Science Series|Bell System Science Series]] incited her interest in science, especially [[The Bell System Science Series#The Strange Case of the Cosmic Rays (1957)|The Strange Case of the Cosmic Rays]] and [[The Bell System Science Series#Hemo the magnificent (1957)|Hemo the magnificent]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Pat Reiff|url=https://multiverse.ssl.berkeley.edu/Solar-Week/Meet-the-Scientists/Pat-Reiff|website=Multiverse.ssl.berkeley.edu|access-date=2021-07-21}}</ref> Her interest in space science began with a father-daughter course at the Oklahoma City Planetarium while she was a Brownie.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Reiff Receives 2013 Space Physics and Aeronomy Richard Carrington Award|url=https://honors.agu.org/sfg-awardees/reiff-receives-2013-space-physics-and-aeronomy-richard-carrington-award/|access-date=2021-07-21|website=Honors.agu.org|language=en-US}}</ref> In college, she started as a math major and did a summer research experience at [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name=":4" /> She started taking classes in astronomy and obtained her B.S. in physics from [[Oklahoma State University System|Oklahoma State University]] (1971).<ref name=":3" /> She moved to [[Rice University]] where she earned an M.S. space science in 1974 working on [[Magnetosheath]] electrons.<ref>{{OCLC|1081448169}}</ref> In 1975 she finished her Ph.D. in space and astronomy working on Apollo plasma data.<ref>{{OCLC|3584757}}</ref> From 1975 to 1976, she worked on [[Explorer 51|Atmosphere Explorer]] data as a National Research Council fellow at [[Marshall Space Flight Center]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SMD Education :: Profile :: Patricia Reiff|url=https://smdepo.org/user/103|access-date=2021-07-22|website=Smdepo.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reiff|first1=P. H.|last2=Hill|first2=T. W.|last3=Burch|first3=J. L.|date=1977|title=Solar wind plasma injection at the dayside magnetospheric cusp|url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/JA082i004p00479|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research|language=en|volume=82|issue=4|pages=479–491|doi=10.1029/JA082i004p00479|bibcode=1977JGR....82..479R|issn=2156-2202|url-access=subscription}}</ref> As of 2021, she is a professor in physics and astronomy at Rice University.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Patricia H. Reiff {{!}} Faculty {{!}} The People of Rice {{!}} Rice University|url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/patricia-h-reiff|access-date=2021-07-21|website=Profiles.rice.edu}}</ref>

{{Blockquote|text=What I like most about my job is the fact that when you discover or figure something out, for that time you are the ONLY one in the world who knows that!|author=Patricia Reiff|source=Interview with Multiverse<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://multiverse.ssl.berkeley.edu/Solar-Week/Meet-the-Scientists/Pat-Reiff|title = Pat Reiff|website=Multiverse.ssl.berkeley.edu}}</ref>}}

== Career ==
Reiff started graduate school at Rice University in 1971 and immediately learned the computer programming needed to work on data from the [[Charged Particle Lunar Environment Experiment]] (CPLEE).<ref name=":4" /> In 2019 she described the process of analyzing data that arrived on 7-track tape reels and then, starting with [[Apollo 15]], being able to watch data arriving in real-time.<ref name=":4" /> In the years following her Ph.D., Reiff worked on data from multiple missions including the [[Dynamics Explorer]], Polar, [[IMAGE (spacecraft)|IMAGE]], and Cluster Missions.<ref name=":1" />

From 1993 until 1998, Reiff served on the NASA Space Science Advisory Committee, and in this role influenced the National Aeronautics and Space Agency (NASA) of the importance of including education and public outreach within science missions.<ref name=":5" /> In subsequent years, she worked on the education and outreach teams for multiple missions, including [[IMAGE (spacecraft)|Imager for Magnetopause to Aurora Global Exploration]] (IMAGE) mission and the [[Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission]] (MMS).<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Eather|first1=Robert E.|last2=Reiff|first2=Patricia Hofer|date=2009|title=Reiff Receives 2009 Athelstan Spilhaus Award|journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union|language=en|volume=90|issue=26|pages=225–226|doi=10.1029/2009EO260008|bibcode=2009EOSTr..90..225E|issn=2324-9250|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Reiff established multiple programs to engage the public in science, including a program on a master of science teaching degree.<ref name=":0" /> She develops software that is disseminated to public education groups and these programs have been seen by over a million visitors at 15 museums,<ref name=":5" /> and she is particularly focused on people in under-served communities in the American southwest.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /> At the Houston Museum of Science, she worked with Carolyn Sumners on digital shows within planetariums,<ref name=":3" /> educational experiences that were ultimately spun off into two commercial ventures.<ref name=":5" /> Reiff also engages the public with real-time [[space weather]] alerts that provided predictions about aurora viewing.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bala|first1=Ramkumar|last2=Reiff|first2=Patricia|date=2012|title=Improvements in short-term forecasting of geomagnetic activity|url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/2012SW000779|journal=Space Weather|language=en|volume=10|issue=6|article-number=2012SW000779 |pages=n/a|doi=10.1029/2012SW000779|bibcode=2012SpWea..10.6001B|issn=1542-7390|hdl=1911/70682|s2cid=13710159 |hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Reiff is a ham radio operator with the call sign W5TAR and has written guidelines to use ham radio to train teachers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=W5TAR Callsign Page|url=https://www.qrz.com/db/W5TAR|access-date=2021-07-23|website=Qrz.com|language=en-US}}</ref> Reiff sponsored the United States' first team to the [[International Astronomy Olympiad]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Extensions of Remarks - December 09, 2019|url=https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record/2019/12/09/extensions-of-remarks-section/article/E1558-4|website=United States Congress|language=en-US}}</ref>

Reiff served as the editor of solar-planetary news in EOS, the journal of the [[American Geophysical Union]], from 1986 to 1989.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Reiff|first=Patricia H.|date=1989|title=Final thanks from the former Editor|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/89EO00101|journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union|language=en|volume=70|issue=13|pages=194|doi=10.1029/89EO00101|bibcode=1989EOSTr..70..194R|issn=0096-3941|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2000, Reiff was the founding director of the Rice Space Institute.<ref>{{cite web|title=RSI Leadership|url=https://rsi.rice.edu/rsi-leadership|website=Rsi.rice.edu|language=en}}</ref>[[File:SPAC-Chairs.jpg|thumb|Patricia Reiff (far right) with chairs of the Space Physics and Astronomy Department at Rice University. From left:  [[Alexander J. Dessler]], Barry Dunning, Umbelina Cantú (Department Administrator), Ronald F. Stebbings, [[F. Curtis Michel]], Jon Weisheit, Patricia Reiff.|alt=Reiff (on right) with chairs of department at Rice]]

== Research ==
Reiff's research is on [[Magnetosphere|magnetospheric physics]] where she works on the aurora<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Artikkel: The Birkeland Lectures|url=http://english.dnva.no/c42031/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27376|access-date=2021-07-21|website=English.dnva.no}}</ref> and how the solar wind changes Earth's environment.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Reiff|first1=P. H.|last2=Hill|first2=T. W.|last3=Burch|first3=J. L.|date=1977|title=Solar wind plasma injection at the dayside magnetospheric cusp|url=https://doi.org/10.1029/JA082i004p00479|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research|language=en|volume=82|issue=4|pages=479–491|doi=10.1029/JA082i004p00479|bibcode=1977JGR....82..479R|issn=2156-2202|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She used high- and low-altitude spacecraft data to show that auroras are caused by the alignment between an electric field and a magnetic field.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reiff|first1=P. H.|last2=Collin|first2=H. L.|last3=Craven|first3=J. D.|last4=Burch|first4=J. L.|last5=Winningham|first5=J. D.|last6=Shelley|first6=E. G.|last7=Frank|first7=L. A.|last8=Friedman|first8=M. A.|date=1988|title=Determination of auroral electrostatic potentials using high- and low-altitude particle distributions|url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/JA093iA07p07441|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics|language=en|volume=93|issue=A7|pages=7441–7465|doi=10.1029/JA093iA07p07441|issn=2156-2202|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
